title: FSAE — GPS Antenna Mount
goal: Construct a GPS antenna, mount it lighter and more stable.
details: Designed a lightweight GPS antenna mount for Formula SAE packaging constraints. The part was FEA-validated in SolidWorks, then 3D printed and mounted with three frame contact points for improved stiffness versus the previous two-point design.
outcome: Fully 3D printed
30% reduction in weight from the original
3 points of contact to the frame rather than 2 on the original
technical: Used SolidWorks FEA to determine stress limitations on the part and evaluate the amount of removable material.

title: Rival Robotics — Double Four-Bar Linkage
goal: Design a low-cost double four-bar linkage.
outcome: Low cost using only Polycard and 3D printed parts
Weight-reduced plates for less moving mass
technical: Fully functional four-bar linkage based on extension limits using a single motor for extension.

title: Freshman Design Project — LEGO Set
goal: Construct a full LEGO set in SolidWorks using Excel for different part configurations.
outcome: A 240-piece LEGO Technic set
60+% of the parts are configurable
Advanced understanding of SolidWorks Part Studio
technical: Several configurable properties for the table enable the easy assembly of over 40 unique parts, reducing CAD time by more than 200% by eliminating the need to construct parts individually.

title: Rival Robotics — Shuttlecock Extraction System
goal: Make a system to extract shuttlecocks from a tube.
outcome: 3 DOF system able to extract at any angle
Easy implementation with the rest of the robot
Fully 3D printed and easily assembleable
Master Sketch can easily change major values and auto-rebuild
technical: Uses a 3 DOF system powered by 2 servos for exact rotation, plus 1 motor to spin the roller bars. Uses an embossed hex shape through a bearing connecting to an insert into the tube to transmit power without running a shaft or external systems.

title: Rival Robotics — Omnidirectional Chassis
goal: Make a rigid and sturdy chassis using omnidirectional wheels to control the robot's movement.
outcome: Easily machinable aluminum plates
Sheet metal parts to reduce complexity and hardware
CNC motor mount as both rigid mounting system and heat sink
technical: Dead axle wheel system for smooth rotation on bearings. Wheels powered via 4 brushless motors with belts. 3D printing for extra parts to reduce machining complexity.

title: 1 lb 3D Printed Battle Bot
goal: Make a 1 lb 3D printed battle bot.
outcome: Modular, easy-swap armor system
Custom resin cast wheels
Easily assembled using heat-set inserts
Custom fully balanced drum with interlocking motor connection for maximum torque output
technical: Fully 3D printed vertical drum spinner. 4-wheel belt drive in rear. Custom wheel molds with draft angles for easy removal. All parts designed from scratch.

title: WCP Cadathon — 3 DOF Arm Gearbox
goal: Make a 3 DOF arm gearbox.
outcome: Fully custom gearbox plates
55:1 gearbox to supply a surplus of torque
technical: Uses a combination of chains and gears to supply the load from the motors to the arm assembly.

title: WCP Cadathon — Basketball Intake
goal: Develop a unique intake for basketballs.
outcome: Compact end effector
Unique gear stacking for a compact design
technical: Uses a NEO Vortex motor for through-shaft capability, sandwiched inside the intake to reduce part and assembly complexity.

title: WCP Cadathon — Ball Launcher & Picker
goal: Create a system to launch small 6" plastic balls and pick them up off the ground.
outcome: Turreted shooter with circular rack and pinion for hood angle
1 motor to actuate all belts in the hopper up to the feeder
Weight-reduced aluminum plates for lower COG and moving mass
1 motor to power the entire intake subsystem
technical: 2 NEO 550 outrunner motors for the shooter hood; many angles for autonomous vision. Belts and gears on a Kraken motor to reduce electronics for the intake.

title: Rival Robotics — Arm System
goal: Create an arm system with complete freedom of motion to place objects in specific locations easily.
outcome: Differential gearbox for X and Z-axis rotation
Virtual 4-bar so input stays in place regardless of arm orientation
QDD motors with 3 Nm torque
Weight-reduced plates to lower CG for vertically extending system
technical: Single shaft with dead and live axles at one pivot so the differential can rotate while a stationary pulley rotates in X but is unaffected by Z rotation.

title: FRC — Cone & Cube Intake
goal: Create a system to pick up small cones and 10" inflatable cubes off the ground.
outcome: Pneumatic-powered extension to reduce complexity
Single high-torque motor for maximum grip
Mostly Lexan construction to reduce weight
Configurable master sketch for geometry and plate design
technical: Through shafts resist torsion on the intake. Small aluminum scab plates on intake arms for compression strength.

title: FRC Robotics Competition — Full Robot
goal: Create a system to score game pieces and navigate the field effectively. Team project of 4.
outcome: Swerve modules: 15 ft/s and omnidirectional movement
Robust rigid elevator system
Specific electronic placement to maximize CG location
technical: Belly pan for critical electronics with integrated cable management. Wire paths zip-tied and constrained to reduce electrical faults.

title: Sophomore Design — Gearbox Design
goal: Design a functional gearbox to meet course load, packaging, and manufacturability requirements.
outcome: Complete CAD gearbox assembly with defined gear ratios
Packaging optimized for mounting and serviceability
Design prepared for fabrication and validation
technical: Used SolidWorks for part modeling, assembly mates, and detail drawings; iterated gear selection and shaft support layout for torque transmission and durability.

title: Sophomore Design — Tensile Testing Rig
goal: Design a tensile testing rig capable of applying controlled load and capturing specimen response.
outcome: Structural frame designed for stiffness under tensile load
Specimen fixturing sized for consistent alignment
CAD package ready for build and lab use
technical: Modeled load path, fixture interfaces, and frame members in SolidWorks with attention to alignment, safety factors, and ease of specimen swap.

title: Junior Design — Robot
goal: Design and develop a junior design robot to satisfy competition/course performance requirements.
outcome: Integrated mechanical subsystems for mobility and manipulation
CAD-driven packaging for electronics and actuators
Design iterated for reliability and manufacturability
technical: Developed full-robot CAD with attention to drive layout, structural rigidity, and subsystem interfaces for assembly and testing.

title: Formula Student — Bell Crank FEA
goal: Analyze a suspension bell crank under expected race loads to validate strength and stiffness.
outcome: FEA study completed for critical load cases
High-stress regions identified and redesigned
Weight reduced while maintaining structural margins
technical: Applied SolidWorks Simulation to evaluate stress, displacement, and factor of safety; used results to refine geometry and material/section choices.

title: Sophomore Design — Bracket FEA Analysis
goal: Perform FEA on a structural bracket to verify it meets strength requirements under design loads.
outcome: Mesh and boundary conditions established for representative loading
Peak stress and deflection quantified
Design recommendations produced from simulation results
technical: Used SolidWorks Simulation for static structural analysis, interpreting stress plots and displacement to guide geometry updates.

title: Formula Student — Brake Rotor Manufacturing
goal: Develop and manufacture a brake rotor suited to Formula Student thermal and packaging constraints.
outcome: Rotor geometry designed for cooling and mass targets
Manufacturing process defined for production of race parts
Part integrated with existing brake package
technical: Combined CAD design with manufacturing planning (stock selection, machining, and finishing) to produce a race-ready rotor.

title: Formula Student — Bladed ARB Design
goal: Design a bladed anti-roll bar (ARB) to tune roll stiffness for Formula Student handling targets.
outcome: Bladed ARB geometry sized for adjustable roll stiffness
Mounting and packaging validated in vehicle CAD
Design balanced stiffness goals with mass and durability
technical: Modeled blade geometry and attachment interfaces in SolidWorks; iterated stiffness/mass tradeoffs for vehicle dynamics targets.

title: Formula Student — MoTeC Workbook
goal: Build a MoTeC workbook/data workflow to support Formula Student vehicle setup and event analysis.
outcome: Structured workbook for logging and reviewing key channels
Faster post-run analysis for setup changes
Repeatable process for team data review
technical: Configured channel layout, math channels, and comparison views to turn raw MoTeC data into actionable engineering decisions.
